title: DR1 lets a trader add a new address from every address picker and from the contact page; the frontend gives them no way to add an address anywhere in the notification journey.

finding.frontend: Every picker ends with one button, Save and continue, and the table above it lists only what the address book already holds (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/_address-picker.njk:69-111). fe-address-picker-place-of-origin shows the search box, the five-row table, the pagination and Save and continue, with no add control between them. The contact page is the same: thirteen radios and the save actions, nothing else (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/contact/template.njk:11-24). The address-book service states the position outright — "This service reads and never writes. The notification journey selects from the organisation's book; adding, changing and removing the records in it belongs to the INS frontend" (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:17-19) — and both pages' tests assert `createAddressHref` is undefined. So a trader who reaches a picker and finds their consignor is not in the book has nowhere to go from this service: they cannot finish the notification without leaving it, and nothing on the page tells them where to leave it to.
finding.prototype: Every picker carries a secondary button, "Add a new address", between the results table and Save and continue (app/views/consignment-address-select.html:161-165). It goes to the address book's add flow carrying the party it was launched from; on completion the new record is written into that party's answer — so the trader comes back with it already selected — and a success banner is rendered at the top of the picker (:30-38). The contact page states the same route in a sentence: "If the correct address is not shown, add a new branch address, then return to this page." (app/views/contact-address-for-consignment.html:64-66).
finding.difference: Give the trader a way out of the dead end at the point they hit it: an "Add a new address" action on each of the five pickers and on the contact page. DR1's own shape is add-then-return-preselected with a success banner, which is what to build towards, and it needs a write path this service does not currently have — the frontend's address-book client is read-only by decision, and creation belongs to the INS front-door. This workspace has since accepted the opposite of that for now: the missing signpost is a deliberate temporary measure, and traders needing a new address hop across to the address book by themselves. So the finding names a gap against DR1 that is real and currently accepted, and the work behind it starts at a signpost naming where to go and how to get back, then reaches DR1's behaviour only with the cross-app link and the return contract. What the finding does not license is treating the bare picker as a defect to fix next.
finding.falsifiedBy: Any control on a frontend picker or on the contact page that leads to adding an address, or any sentence on either page naming where to add one.
finding.correction: Premise verified; one sentence about the accepted decision was inverted and is rewritten. The premise — that the frontend has no create-address page at all, so there is no return hand-off left to compare — holds. Searching the whole frontend source for every spelling of an add-address route, link or href turns up two hits and both are tests asserting absence: the picker controller test asserts `createAddressHref` is undefined for all five parties, and the contact controller test asserts both `createAddressHref` and an `addNewAddress` copy string are undefined. The address routes are two, a GET and a POST on the picker path, with no third. The rendered picker and contact pages carry no such control. DR1's side is observable rather than inferred: the picker renders "Add a new address" as a secondary button linking to /address-book/add?from=place-of-origin, and the contact page renders the sentence with "add a new branch address" linking to /address-book/add?from=contact-address. The inverted sentence was "the interim accepted in this workspace is that traders hop across manually, which makes the minimum change a signpost". The accepted decision of 19 August says the reverse — the missing signpost itself is accepted as the temporary measure, superseding the sequencing note that had the cross-app link landing first. That does not falsify the finding, which is a parity statement against DR1, but it does change what done means, so the slot now says so.

relatedTo.why: both are links out of the picker into the address book, and both are settled by the same decision about which service owns address records
